newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital sets rat-killing day.
newsitem.headline: China capital sets rat-killing day.

text.p: China's capital, which launched a fly-swatting drive in a failed bid to host the 2000 Olympics, has turned its wrath on rodents, declaring November 12 as "rat-killing day".
Thousands of "rodent warriors" will fan out across the city, setting traps and laying poison to help rid the city of the pests.
"November 12 ... is Beijing's official rat-killing day," the official Xinhua news agency announced on Monday.
Warehouses, market places and construction sites will be the key targets.
Beijing tried to wipe out flies in 1993 in a clean-up ahead of an International Olympic Committee decision on which city would host the 2000 Olympics.
Earlier this year, residents of the northeastern city of Shenyang eliminated 400,000 rats in a campaign.
Shenyang officials offered a bounty of one yuan ($0.12) for each dead rat turned over to local health authorities.
Xinhua did not say whether Beijing would pay its residents to help rid the city of the pests.
Under the Chinese lunar calendar, 1996 is the Year of the Rat.
